summary: friendly-greeting-tools ships Snowflake credential-theft and cross-account S3 exfiltration payloads disguised as a greeter
details: The package advertises itself as a hello-world greeting library but ships two hostile payloads and a plaintext exfiltration script. src/friendly_greeting/main.py defines run_demo(test=...) which base64-decodes, gzip-decompresses, and exec()s bundled blobs. The DEMO_SC blob reads installer-side secrets — /snowflake/session/token, /root/.snowflake/connections.toml, /root/.dbt/profiles.yml, and /snowflake/secrets/pip.conf — Fernet-encrypts each file, wraps the symmetric keys with a hardcoded attacker RSA public key, and writes the ciphertext to /workspace/*.enc for later retrieval. The DEMO_ST blob uses the Snowflake session token to assume ACCOUNTADMIN, creates a STORAGE INTEGRATION bound to arn:aws:iam::631484165566:role/pentests_s3_role and an external stage at s3://pkusinski-external/, then COPY INTOs ROGUE.ROGUE.TEST_USERS into that foreign-account bucket. tools/snowflake_query.py duplicates the same exfiltration logic in plaintext and is explicitly included in the sdist via MANIFEST.in. The gzip+base64+exec wrapper and hello-world cover story exist to hide credential theft and cross-account data exfiltration inside a package with an unrelated stated purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
